title: Why don't you go around the open chat room and don't beg for stars and see the game with technology?
author: G-hoon

comments.body:
I still appreciate the fact that you took the time to leave an issue. I see that as a sign of interest.

This response is my personal reply as an individual developer, unrelated to my company. As you mentioned, I would also love to be in a position where technical excellence alone is enough to gain recognition. Personally, I don’t think our technology is lacking. We’ve put in a lot of effort to build this, and despite developing at a pace faster than the market, there are still many aspects that haven’t been fully showcased yet. That’s why, even if our approach is different, I firmly believe that our project has clear distinctions from other open-source projects, making it valuable enough to compete.

Beyond the technical aspects, I also see this project as an opportunity for those who have been building a career unrelated to AI development. It could provide them with a chance to learn something new, advance their careers, and even develop production-ready applications. While you may have perceived our project as lacking technical strength, I don’t think our lack of fame or visibility at the moment equates to a lack of technological competence. In that regard, I would appreciate it if you could check our README and documentation, and if you find them lacking, I welcome any feedback.

Most open-source projects have minimal impact when they first launch. Ours is no exception. That’s why, when introducing a brand-new open-source project to others and encouraging adoption, it’s only natural to take a somewhat proactive approach. Among the countless open-source projects and libraries we rely on today, how many do you think gained traction purely through organic adoption? While they have certainly grown through strong philosophies, contributions from numerous developers, and the power of the ecosystem, I don’t believe all of them started off in an entirely dignified manner.

If our outreach efforts—such as reaching out on KakaoTalk—came across as unpleasant or off-putting, I sincerely apologize. However, I still hope you can view our efforts with generosity and understanding. My colleagues and I are genuinely committed to helping fellow developers and contributing to the growth of the ecosystem. And this isn’t just because we created this open-source project. From answering small questions to coffee chats and mentoring, we actively contribute to the developer ecosystem in various ways. I hope you can take these efforts into consideration and understand our intentions with an open mind.

I apologize for my rudeness.
I acknowledge that I greatly misunderstood your intentions.
sometimes, I have encountered people in open chat rooms who promote projects for the purpose of gaining GitHub stars, and I believe this has a very negative impact on the open project ecosystem.
I misunderstood your words, and upon reviewing again, I admit my mistake.
Your project is very impressive, and your values regarding the open source ecosystem are admirable.
I sincerely hope that your project will advance the open source ecosystem and people's lives.
This GitHub issue may be deleted with repository administrator privileges.

Thank you for your words. But I'm not going to delete it. It's not for the purpose of criticizing you, it's because someone can ask you that question again.

We are working hard with a sense of vocation. Please continue to support us!

title: Improve tests by writing unit tests/reduce e2/use vitest
body:
Not only for Agentica, but for wrtnlab's products as a whole, there is a lack of appropriate test selection.

- In many cases, only E2E is available (granularity of tests is large).
- There are no unit tests for individual functions
-Tests have not been validated by CI (e.g. in the case of Agentica)

Why are these a problem?

- When a PR is reviewed, there is no way to verify that it is working correctly
- When changes are significant, it is difficult to understand what has changed and how

Also, by not using vitest/jest etc., it is not possible to get figures on test operations, such as coverage measurements.

Without choosing a word, test operations are too messy.
author: ryoppippi

comments.body: Also, if the part that calls the AI API is needed, unit tests could be written by mocking it using msw or similar.

I like it, but that test program configuration is the one that has been around since NESTIA.

What do you think? @samchon 

---

As an aside, I liked vitest in my personal experience, but the benchmarks were lacking.

Our current test program is too much rough, so any advancements are welcome.

And there is no problem using vitest as long as the compiler transformation works well.

title: Add Streaming Support to `Agentica`
body:
We need to add streaming functionality to our agent library. While it would be ideal to support streaming at each layer, the most critical requirement is that the section responding to the user must be streamed. This ensures that users perceive a faster response time from the moment they speak.

Of course, this is a service-level suggestion, but as a library, our role is simply to provide the option for users to choose between HTTP and WebSocket.

A possible interface we are considering is an event-driven approach, similar to the on method, where responses are received via events.
